subject: Draft: Deal GPU phasing, on-call warmup & escrow windows
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@lyriatech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Deal GPU phasing, on-call warmup & escrow windows

Claire — attaching a revised proposal and the demand profile you shared. High level ask: we want to lock a predictable baseline for Lyriatech while giving you the ability to burst. To avoid surprises on both sides, we've sketched an activation ladder and a short on-call warmup schedule for critical launches.

Key points in the attached PDF: 
- Baseline (minimum) lane: 24 GPUs reserved dedicated for persistent inference capacity.
- Escrow / step-up windows: monthly review with 14-day activation lead for +16 GPU bursts (subject to availability).
- Ramp schedule: Month 1: 24 GPUs; Month 3: +8 GPUs pre-allocated as a warm reserve; Month 6: revisit to reach 48 GPUs target depending on usage.
- On-call warmup: pre-warm windows (2x 2-hour slots per week) for KV cache priming ahead of major commits.

Could you confirm whether procurement needs additional language for a soft-decommit (60 days) or a literal minimum-term non-decommit clause? Also flagged the parts where finance asked for a burn-credit structure — that's in the spreadsheet.

Next step: if this structure looks directionally right, Karthik can put together an activation-runbook (prewarm playbook + SLOs) for legal and your engineering team.

Thanks — Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal summary, pricing ladder), lyriatech_demand_profile.xlsx (usage forecast)

From: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@lyriatech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@lyriatech.com>, Lyriatech Procurement <procurement@lyriatech.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Deal GPU phasing, on-call warmup & escrow windows

Jonas — thanks for the clear write-up. A few immediate items from our side: 

1) Procurement prefers a 90-day soft-decommit notice rather than 60 if possible; finance wants a mid-term review instead of an automatic step-up at Month 6.
2) We need to understand the failure/fallback policy if Redwood cannot fulfill a burst request within that 14-day window. Is there automatic fallback to a lower-latency hosted model or credits?
3) Engineering: the on-call warmup slots are useful — can you clarify expected warm start time (i.e., how long before peak traffic should we trigger prewarm to see KV hit-rate benefits)?

Marco from procurement is looped for legal language. We also pushed the demand spreadsheet through our internal modeler — attached a brief comment column.

Claire
VP Product, Lyriatech
claire.thompson@lyriatech.com

---
Attachment: lyriatech_demand_profile.xlsx (Claire's commented version)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@lyriatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Deal GPU phasing, on-call warmup & escrow windows

Claire / Jonas — quick technical responses inline: 

1) Fallbacks: we recommend two fallbacks, ordered by preference: 
   a) Auto-fallback to a compatible quantized model variant in the same region (lower-cost path) with routed traffic;
   b) As a last resort, automatic routing to Redwood-hosted multi-tenant endpoint with guaranteed SLA credits for any latency degradation.
   We can codify the exact credit formula (tokens-per-credit) in the SLA.

2) Warm-start timing: for typical Lyriatech workload shapes in your spreadsheet, empirical warming to reach 70–80% of steady-state KV hit-rate is ~90–120 minutes of sustained warm traffic at 10% of peak QPS. The two weekly 2-hour warm windows are a conservative baseline; for major launches we'd recommend an extended 4-hour priming window 24 hours before cutover.

3) Soft-decommit: 90-day window is operationally manageable, though it changes our buffer planning. If procurement wants 90 days, we propose adding a short decommit fee (1 month of baseline spend) to keep the capacity pool healthy during the trailing window.

I will draft a short activation-runbook and include the fallback routing matrices. Jonas — want me to include projected cost delta for a 90-day vs 60-day notice?

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@lyriatech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@lyriatech.com>, Lyriatech Procurement <procurement@lyriatech.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Deal GPU phasing, on-call warmup & escrow windows

Karthik — thanks, that helps. From procurement/legal: 

- We are okay with fallback routing as long as we get a clear credit schedule and an escalation SLA (phone/email) for any failed bursts.
- Decommit: 90 days acceptable if Redwood adds the 1-month bridge fee AND we get a clawback on unused committed credits after 12 months (pro-rated).

Operational ask: can Redwood include a calendarized ramp commitment table in the contract (example below) so our ops team has a deterministic activation plan? 

Requested calendarized ramp (example):
- Effective Date (T): baseline 24 GPUs active
- T+60 days: +8 GPUs allocated (warm reserve)
- T+180 days: +16 GPUs (conditional on 75% of forecast CPU/GPU utilization for 30 days)
- T+365 days: target 48 GPUs (subject to mutual review)

Please include trigger-language for the conditional steps. Also request a 30-day notice for scheduling pre-warm slots that are outside the weekly recurring windows (we need predictable calendar blocks).

Marco
Director, Procurement — Lyriatech

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@lyriatech.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@lyriatech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Deal GPU phasing, on-call warmup & escrow windows

Marco / Claire — appreciate the concrete asks, good alignment. Summary / next steps: 

1) We will accept 90-day soft-decommit with a 1-month bridge fee and a 12-month pro-rated clawback on unused committed credits (language to be provided by Legal).
2) Redwood will publish a calendarized ramp table in the Statement of Work and include trigger language for conditional allocations (75% utilization over 30 days).
3) Fallback credit formula & escalation SLA: Karthik will share a proposed credits schedule and a draft escalation ladder (P1/P2 contact windows).
4) Pre-warm scheduling: Redwood accepts a 30-day notice for non-recurring pre-warm blocks; weekly recurring 2x 2-hour slots remain at no extra charge.

I'll get Finance and Legal to push a redline of the proposal (redwood_proposal_v2.pdf) to you by EOD Friday. If that timeline works I'll schedule a short 30-minute call for Monday to walk the runbook with Lyriatech ops and engineering.

Thanks — moving to finalize.

Jonas
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments referenced earlier: redwood_proposal_v2.pdf, lyriatech_demand_profile.xlsx
